vintage.installations: OpenStreetMap, as of the download date

rule: A city gets an Encampment when its former province holds a major installation (10 km²+), a naval base or a military airfield: a fortress with two or more of them, else a garrison.

rules.installations: Every OpenStreetMap feature in Vietnam tagged as military land (landuse=military or a military=* tag), except trenches, bunkers, checkpoints and offices; unnamed ones only from 1 km². Several features in one hex and branch are folded into the largest.
rules.tier: major: outline of 10 km² or more; base: 1 km² or more; site: smaller or no outline. By area only: no headcount is published.
rules.components: Branch from the tags and names: naval bases, 'Hải quân', 'Quân cảng', 'Hải đoàn' → Navy; airfields, 'Sân bay', 'Không quân', 'Phòng không', 'Tên lửa', 'Ra đa' → Air Defence – Air Force; 'Biên phòng', 'Cảnh sát biển' → Border guard & other; the rest → Ground forces.
rules.ranges: Outlines of 5 km² or more (firing ranges, training areas, large bases) are drawn as restricted ground on the hexes whose centre they cover.
rules.encampment: A city gets an Encampment when its former province holds a major installation (10 km²+), a naval base or a military airfield: a fortress with two or more of them, else a garrison.

caveats: OpenStreetMap is a volunteer map: coverage is uneven, many military areas are unmapped or unnamed, and some names are generic ('Doanh trại'). Vietnam publishes no installation list, troop numbers or defence spending by province, so troop, spending and veteran figures are left empty: never estimated.
